narr: The region was under the influence of a warm, moist airmass due to a southeast CONUS ridge allowing for ample Gulf moisture return northward into the southern Great Lakes. A weak stationary boundary was focused from west to east across northern OH during the afternoon and evening of the 10th. Loosely organized convection formed along the boundary, with efficient warm rain processed due to surface dewpoints near 70F, PWAT values ranging from 1.7 to 1.9 across the region, and modest MLCAPE values near 1000 j/kg. Steering flow was weak under the ridge, with slow, generally westward moving storms. A more organized cluster of convection trained generally along a Marion to Mansfield to southern Medina to southern Summit county line during the early evening hours, where 1 to 3 inches of rain fell in a 1 to 3 hour period.
ev: Numerous roads were inundated and closed in and around downtown Lodi due to excessive runoff from heavy rainfall. Reports of numerous basements flooded, with some reports of vehicle damage as well.
Resident of Chippewa Lake shared photographs of flooding around the Chippewa Lake Amusement Park area, with several feet of standing water up to residences with one vehicle damaged.
lsr: NUMEROUS ROAD CLOSURES AROUND THE CITY OF LODI WITH SEVERAL REPORTS OF WATER IN BASEMENTS OF HOUSES.
